Data Science Tools (WS 2025/26)

Chapter 6 RStudio

6.1 RStudio screen

RStudio is an extremely powerful Integrated Development Environment (IDE) developed by Posit, with which you develop software and carry out data analyses. Beyond this RStudio also contains tools and interfaces for documentation (e.g. RMarkdown and Quarto), project management, environment control, version control (e.g. Github), databases (via connections and libraries) and package development. R support many tools including dashboards (Shiny17), interfaces to other programming languages such as Python using reticulate, C++ using Rcpp and others, formatting systems like LaTeX and Markdown and Large Language Models (LLM) like Github Copilot. All these tools are well integrated into RStudio.

Please note: Posit has recently developed an IDE called Positron, which makes it easier to work with both R and Python simultaneously. However, a whole range of tools that are already available in a mature and stable form in RStudio are still missing, while Positron is still in its infancy (beta testing). For this reason, RStudio will still be used in this course in the 2025/26 winter semester. In the medium term, however, a switch to Positron might be a good option.

Positron emphasizes data analysis. Contrary to Positron the RStudio IDE in its current state is additionally also a very capable for the development of statistical software.

6.2 RStudio elements

RStudio has numerous shortcuts. However, a small subset of all shortcuts and commands is sufficient for meaningful use.

  • Header bar (with elements such as File, Edit, Code, View, Plots, Session, Build, Debug, Profile, Tools, Help) as well as partially context-sensitive buttons under the header bar and in subwindows (e.g. the STOP button in the console, which is only active during computing).

  • Configurable panel fields (Panes, can be set under Tools \(\rightarrow\) Global Options\(\rightarrow\) Pane Layout). The most important are the following Panes, between which you can quickly switch using keyboard sequences.

    1. Source (Ctrl+1)
    2. Console (Ctrl+2)
    3. Help (Ctrl+3)
    4. Show history (Ctrl+4)
    5. Show files (Ctrl+5)
    6. Show plots (Ctrl+6)
    7. Show packages (Ctrl+7)
    8. Show environment (Ctrl+8)
    9. Show viewer (Ctrl+9)

Attention:

Ctrl+digit means that the Ctrl key (Ctrl key) and the associated key with the corresponding digit (but not the function key) are pressed together.

If you want to maximize the corresponding window, you usually add Shift. However, this does not always work, e.g. Ctrl+Shift+1 maximizes the source code panel, but Ctrl+Shift+2 does not maximize the console, but restores the configuration with the usual fourfold window division – unless the cursor is already in the console. According to the help, the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+Alt+0 should actually be used to restore this window division, but this does not always work in a German-speaking Windows 10 environment. In any case, you can create the desired window division or window expansion by clicking on the four button in the header or by selecting View \(\rightarrow\) Panes \(\rightarrow\) Show all Panes.

Caution: RStudio contains a lot of keyboard shortcuts, so you can quickly cause mischief by mistake. It is therefore advisable to save the source file often and to undo any subsequent incorrect changes successively with Ctrl+Z. K means pressing the K key, i.e. not pressing the capital letter using Shift+k.

6.3 RStudio – the most important panels (panes) and keyboard shortcuts

Preliminary remark:

  1. For the definition of panes see the Wikipedia entry List of graphical user interface elements.

  2. Depending on the keyboard driver and key mapping, some keys may not work. In this case, the corresponding functions must be entered via menus.

  3. The keyboard shortcuts in the list below are only a small, subjective selection of the most useful shortcuts in my opinion. By clicking on the field See All Shortcuts in the help via Help\(\rightarrow\) Keyboard Shortcuts Help you will get a complete and very extensive list.

Keyboard shortcuts (selection):

  • Everywhere (in all panes)
    • Shortcut Help (Alt+Shift+K)
    • Show all Panes (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+0, does not always work under German Windows 10/11)
  • In the panes source code and view
    • Next tab in file or view (Ctrl+Tab)
    • Previous tab in file or view (Ctrl+Shift+Tab)
  • Source (Ctrl+1)
    • New file with File \(\rightarrow\) New File \(\rightarrow\) R Script (Ctrl+Shift+N)
    • Save file under File \(\rightarrow\) Save (Ctrl+s) or Save as
    • Open file under File \(\rightarrow\) Open File (Ctrl+O)
    • Current help for the selected command (F1)
    • Execute current line and move forward (Ctrl+Return)18
    • Execute start to current line (Ctrl+Alt+B)
    • Execute current chunk in RMarkdown (Ctrl+Shift+Return)
    • Restart R, i.e. reinitialize R; incl. detach all loaded libraries (Ctrl+Shift+F10)
    • Assignment symbol (Alt+-) <- (Note: with RMarkdown, the equal sign = is inserted in the text with some RStudio versions)
    • The pipe operator %>% (Ctrl+Shift+M) frequently used in the Tidyverse, explanation follows later. IMPORTANT NOTE: Since R 4.1, the pipe operator |> has been introduced in R, which - with very few exceptions19 - has the same function as the pipe operator %>% defined in the tidyverse in the R package maggrittr. If you want to generate the pipe operator |> implemented in R in RStudio with Ctrl+Shift+M, this must be set under Tools \(\rightarrow\) Global Options \(\rightarrow\) Code \(\rightarrow\) Editing.
    • Partly as usual under Windows cursor and key control (e.g. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V, \(\uparrow\), i.e. arrow-up etc.).
    • Generate HTML report from source with results (Ctrl+Shift+K, only for Rmd and HTML sources)
    • Execute the running script (Ctrl+Shift+S)
    • To gain an overview:
      • Collapse fold (Alt+L)
      • Expand fold (Alt+Shift+L)
      • Collapse all folds (Alt+O)
      • Expand all folds (Alt+Shift+O). Note: Letter ‘O’, not digit ‘0’.
  • Console (bottom left) for program input and output (Ctrl+2)
    • Direct input of R commands possible; execute with Return.
    • Empty console (Ctrl+L)
    • Scroll through the last commands (Ctrl+\(\uparrow\), Ctrl+\(\downarrow\)) and embed the selected code for post-editing with Return.
  • Help (Ctrl+3) allows you to view and search the help; clicking on the home icon takes you to the main window.
    • Entering help.start() in RGui (not RStudio) calls up more convenient help in the external web browser; RStudio uses the internal help window.
    • Entering help.start() in the RStudio console opens the help window and displays the URL at the same time. If you enter this URL in the browser, you will get the same help as calling help.start() in RGui.
  • History (Ctrl+4) allows you to view previous commands and copy them to Source or Console (select and click either To Source or To Console)
  • Show Files (Ctrl+5) allows you to browse and select files and change directories.
  • Show Plots (Ctrl+6) allows you to view graphics, zoom and export.
  • Show Packages (Ctrl+7) allows you to install and update packages and view the documentation by clicking on the name of an R package to call up the corresponding help pages directly.
  • Environment (Ctrl+8) allows you to view variables and functions without entering a console.

Please make sure that you are using the correct R version (currently R 4.4.3) for this course under RStudio. You can set this under Tools \(\rightarrow\) Global Options \(\rightarrow\) Basic \(\rightarrow\) R-Version.

On Posit’s cheat sheet page you will find a scrolable RStudio IDE cheatsheet with the most important commands.as well as its PDF version.
